title: The Storm Peaks
body: The Storm Peaks rise in the northeast of Northrend, a realm of wind-scoured summits, glaciers and frozen valleys, and the highest mountain in Northrend is crowned by the open-sided Temple of Storms. This was the domain of the titans' keepers. At its northern edge stands Ulduar, a titan city of vast halls and terraces, now held by Loken, whose iron dwarves make war on every creature of stone and have driven the earthen from their home. Elsewhere the old pacts lie broken. The frost giants of Dun Niffelem, the Sons of Hodir, feud with the Hyldnir, the vrykul women of Brunnhildar who serve the brooding Thorim, while their sisters at Valkyrion have taken the Lich King's gift. Strangers have come as well: goblin prospectors at K3, the Explorers' League among the frost dwarves of Frosthold, a stranded Horde zeppelin crew at Grom'arsh, and Brann Bronzebeard, chasing the secrets of Ulduar.

title: K3
body: K3 is a goblin town at the southern foot of the Storm Peaks, built by prospectors who came for their share of the titan machines hidden in the mountains. Progress has been slow: the cold freezes the motor of every flier they launch, and trouble presses on every side. Savage Hill gnolls under Gnarlhide steal parts from the town's very doorstep, Tore Rumblewrench's miners have still to clear Crystalweb Cavern of its spiders, and to the northeast the magnataur of Garm and their snobold followers mean to take K3 for themselves. West of town lies Jeer Sparksocket's minefield, watched over by turrets that shoot down anything trying to fly in.

parts.body: A runner set a teleporter up behind Garm, on Garm's Rise, and once its lost power cell had been found and fitted, the way into the magnataur's lair lay open. Gino's goblin sappers now hold the rise and fight in Garm itself, and the brutes have nowhere left to run.

title: Sifreldar Village and the Forlorn Mine
body: Sifreldar Village looks down on K3 from the heights to the north, a settlement of the Hyldnir, the frost vrykul women of the peaks, guarded by storm maidens and runekeepers. Rusty cages hold goblin prisoners and salvaged K3 equipment lies among the longhouses, for the Hyldnir fell on a goblin expedition climbing into the mountains to raise a transmission tower, carried off its men and let the women go. In the north of the village is the entrance to the Forlorn Mine, where captive vrykul men dig under the blades of Hyldnir overseers.

parts.body: The captured goblin men have been freed and are back with Gretchen Fizzlespark, all but one. Her brother Zeev, the others say, is still up in the village, and the Hyldnir keep a mine where they put their prisoners to work.

title: Brunnhildar Village
body: Brunnhildar Village is the stronghold of the Hyldnir, who call themselves the servants of Thorim. Here the women rule and fight, and they hold that whoever wins the Hyldsmeet, their sacred contest of strength, is assured a lifetime at Thorim's side. Challengers spar in the lanes, bear riders school their warbears for the Pit of the Fang, and proto-drakes are kept for the riders of the sky. The Hyldnir are at war with the frost giants of Dun Niffelem, beyond the Valley of Ancient Winters, and they meet any outsider who walks into the village with steel.

parts.body: Wrapped in Lok'lira's illusion, a stranger passes for a battle-sister, and the village opens its doors. Lodge-Matron Embla offers food and rest, Gretta the Arbiter keeps the order of the contests, Astrid Bjornrittar breaks bears for riding, and Iva the Vengeful and Thyra Kvinnshal rage against Valkyrion, whose Hyldnir took the Lich King's offer when Brunnhildar dismembered his emissaries.

title: Valkyrion
body: Valkyrion lies far to the northwest, beyond the Temple of Storms, a Hyldnir village that turned from Thorim. Its people accepted the advances of the Lich King, and those who receive his gift, the val'kyr, fly above the village on feathered wings. Rather than capture their drakes in the wild as their sisters do, the aspirants of Valkyrion raise them from blight: the eggs lie in a fetid pool of plague, and blighted proto-drakes hatch from them. In the largest dwelling lives Yulda the Stormspeaker, the witch who carried the Lich King's promises of power to Brunnhildar.

parts.body: Yulda the Stormspeaker has paid for insulting the Hyldsmeet. A blade sent by Iva the Vengeful found her in the largest dwelling of Valkyrion, and in Brunnhildar they say she had it coming: no one mocks their traditions and lives, not even one of their own.

title: Temple of Storms
body: The Temple of Storms stands open to the winds on the summit of the highest mountain in Northrend, and within it sits Thorim, the Stormlord, alone. He has withdrawn here from the world below and broods in silence, heedless of those who climb to him. Around the peak wheel the proto-drakes of the Hyldnir, their wild kin nest across the Dragonspine Peaks, and on a lesser peak to the southeast lies the Broodmother's Nest, long empty of eggs.

title: Frosthold
body: Frosthold lies in a great pit of ice atop a mountain in the southwest of the peaks, the stronghold of the frostborn, the frost dwarves. They are a warrior people ruled by King Yorg Stormheart, and the stormcrest eagles that nest on the heights above the town are their old allies and their mounts. An Explorers' League expedition under Lagnus has made camp among them, its archaeologists and relic hunters welcomed by their hosts. In the valleys of Bor's Breath to the east, Frostfeather harpies harry the frostborn and their eagles alike.

parts.body: King Stormheart has told his people that he will be leaving them for a time, and he was firm that none of the frostborn should follow him. They respect his wishes, as they always have. Velog Icebellow has taken charge of the clan in his absence, and Frosthold's welcome to its friends still stands.

title: Grom'arsh Crash-Site
body: The Grom'arsh Crash-Site is a Horde camp raised in the wreck of a goblin zeppelin that came down high in the peaks, and its crew has stayed where it fell. Boktar Bloodfury commands here, with the shaman Moteha Windborn and Bloodguard Lorga among his people, and a few grunts keep watch over the broken hull. The cold is the camp's worst enemy, and the crew burns timbers from the wreck to stay alive. Worgs make their lair in Gimorak's Den, a cave east of the camp.

title: The Foot Steppes and the Engine of the Makers
body: The Foot Steppes are hard, open land east of Frosthold, where ice rhinos graze and proto-drakes hunt among the crags. Stormforged trackers prowl them, and in the southeast the Frigid Tomb is held by ancient guardians of ice. In the midst of the steppes the Engine of the Makers, a great pit of titan works, is sunk deep into the ground, and beside it stands a lonely watcher, Creteus, whom the frostborn call the keeper.

parts.body: When Norgannon's Core was lifted from the Frigid Tomb, the steppes erupted. An iron host poured across them, stormforged warmongers and iron behemoths among them, and King Yorg Stormheart and his frostborn axemen met it on the open ground, with Creteus standing among them above the Engine of the Makers.

title: Bouldercrag's Refuge and the Snowdrift Plains
body: Bouldercrag's Refuge is an old titan building on the face of a mountain west of the Inventor's Library, where the earthen expelled from Ulduar have taken shelter. On the Snowdrift Plains below they hold the line against Loken's stormforged and their war golems, with dolomite giants fighting at their side. The irons gain ground inch by inch. Fallen defenders lie in the snow, and the earthen mine what enchanted earth they can from the cliffs to heal them.

title: Nidavelir and Narvir's Cradle
body: Nidavelir is the stronghold of the stormforged iron dwarves, southwest across the Snowdrift Plains from Bouldercrag's Refuge, and Runeseer Valduran commands there, said to hold powerful titan artifacts given him by Loken. On the western side of the plains the irons have dug the Frozen Mine, where captive mechagnomes, servants of Keeper Mimir, haul out cartloads of dark, sickly ore. South of the refuge sprawls Narvir's Cradle, a great construction ground of scaffolds and lightning forges where stormforged artificers labor on a project of Valduran's. Far to the south, Uldis, a titan facility, opens on a mountain above the Bor's Breath River.

parts.body: Loken's gifts to Valduran, the relics called Loken's Fury, Loken's Power and Loken's Favor, have been destroyed in Nidavelir, and the stormforged are weaker for it. They fight on all the same: their own losses mean nothing to them, and Bouldercrag fears they will keep coming until the earthen are pounded to gravel.

title: The Inventor's Library
body: The Inventor's Library stands on the northern coast south of Ulduar, built by Keeper Mimir, the tinker, to hold his work. Its guardians still murmur through diagnostics, data restoration and security protocols among the databanks, and a scrapbot, SCRAP-E, is charged with keeping the consoles in Mimir's absence, though its last maintenance cycle is long overdue. East along the northern mountain face stands Mimir's Workshop, unused for many years, where a few of the keeper's attendants still wait for their next directive.

title: The Valley of Ancient Winters
body: The Valley of Ancient Winters runs east from Brunnhildar Village toward Dun Niffelem, and it is the battlefield of their feud: Hyldnir warbears clash there with the frost giants of Niffelem and their frostworgs. Off the valley opens the Hibernal Cavern, where the Hyldnir long found their best bears, but ravenous jormungar have overrun it and the wild bears are all but gone. On a mountainside above the valley, a round door leads into a titan vault called Loken's Bargain.

parts.body: To Thorim's envoy the valley shows another face. The Sons of Hodir walk it openly, stoic mammoths graze its floor, wild wyrms circle overhead and jormungar roam the snow, and the carcasses of icemaw bears lie where the jormungar left them.

title: Dun Niffelem
body: Dun Niffelem is the city of the frost giants who call themselves the Sons of Hodir, east of the Valley of Ancient Winters, where spikes of ice rise over the giants' halls. The giants are at war with the Hyldnir: proto-drakes taken from Brunnhildar lie chained in the city, and captured Hyldnir warriors stand frozen in blocks of ice where the giants can mock them. The Sons of Hodir were once allies of Thorim, but they have long nursed a hatred of the Stormlord, and strangers are not welcome here lightly.

parts.body: To Thorim's envoy the city opens its halls. King Jokkum holds court here with Lorekeeper Randvir and the frostworg denmother close by, Lillehoff serves as the giants' quartermaster and Calder sells smithing supplies, and in the stronghold looms the frozen image of Arngrim the Insatiable, the old king of the giants.

title: Fjorn's Anvil and Frostfield Lake
body: East of Dun Niffelem glows Fjorn's Anvil, the forge of Fjorn, who has laid siege to the frost giants' city with giants of iron. The anvil is scalding even in the wintry air. Fire revenants, seething with heat, guard it and stalk the shores of Frostfield Lake, where stormforged iron giants march, and the frost giants of Niffelem can do little against them while Fjorn holds his anvil.

parts.body: Since Fjorn fell, the iron giants lie dead on the fields by Frostfield Lake, and the Sons of Hodir have come to claim his anvil. Njormeld oversees the work while frost giant stormheralds breathe cold over its glowing face, cooling it so that it can be carried home.

title: Thunderfall
body: Thunderfall lies northeast of Dun Niffelem, a desolate field of ice where frozen fossils lie half buried in the ground. Little stirs here but the wind and a few tundra rams, and among the fossils lies the body of a fallen frostborn warrior, far from his home. To the frost giants of Dun Niffelem, the place is bound up with a dark memory they have never let go.

parts.body: Thunderfall is not at rest. To those who come in Thorim's cause, the spirits of Niffelem forefathers and of frostborn warriors are plain to see, wandering restless among the ice, and the shattered fragments of a great horn lie scattered in the snow.

title: Camp Tunka'lo
body: Camp Tunka'lo is a village of taunka in the far east of the peaks, beyond the Terrace of the Makers and north of Dun Niffelem, its tents guarded by the camp's braves. Scrolls of the village's history are kept about the camp. To the north lies the Howling Hollow, where the taunka bury their honored elders, and to the northwest Frostfloe Deep, the burial cave of their warriors. Below the camp spreads the Plain of Echoes, where mammoths and rhinos roam, scions of storm ride the wind and the restless spirits of taunka ancestors wander.

title: The Terrace of the Makers
body: The Terrace of the Makers spreads over the high ground northwest of Dun Niffelem toward Ulduar, the sacred grounds of the titans. Temples crown its heights: the Temple of Invention, seat of Keeper Mimir, with the Temples of Winter, Life and Order, and beyond them the Hall of the Shaper and the Temple of Wisdom, the last just southwest of Ulduar. The terrace is a battlefield. Loken's iron dwarves burst from the ground in mole machines with iron sentinels beside them, and the earthen, sworn to guard these grounds with their lives, fight on against them.

parts.body: Loken had not left the terrace to his iron dwarves alone. His most powerful lieutenants held it for him, and Thorim's champion hunted them down with the earthen at the call of the Horn of the Peaks: the giant Eisenfaust in the Hall of the Shaper, then Halefnir the Windborn and Duronn the Runewrought deeper within. One by one, Loken's servants fell.

title: Ulduar
body: Ulduar rises at the northern edge of the Storm Peaks, a titan city of colossal halls, towers and gates, and Loken holds it now. Its earthen makers live in exile, and from its outer works open the Halls of Stone and the Halls of Lightning. On the approach to the city, a trader named Chester Copperpot keeps a camp of general and trade goods under the watch of his hired goons, Slosh sells food and drink beside him, and Shavalius the Fancy keeps a flight master's post for travelers.

parts.body: In time the way into Ulduar opened to the bold. Brann Bronzebeard has led an expedition to the city's gates, where engineers of the Explorers' League and K3 have rebuilt siege engines left by the Alliance and Horde expeditions that came before them. Archmage Pentarus, who helped fund the venture, and the mages of the Kirin Tor shield their platform. What waits within is for those who follow to learn.

title: Thorim
body: Thorim, the Stormlord, is a being of near godlike stature who served the titans as guardian of Ulduar and the Terrace of the Makers. Now he sits alone in the Temple of Storms, sunk in a grief so deep that he barely heeds those who climb to him, while far below the Hyldnir compete in the Hyldsmeet for the honor of a lifetime at his side. What broke him he does not tell to strangers.

parts.body: Thorim's grief is for his wife, Sif, slain by his own brother. He was sworn to guard the pacts between the races of frost as well as the titans' grounds, yet his brother tricked him into blaming Sif's death on a dear friend, Arngrim, king of the frost giants, and he turned on his allies. When he saw what he had done, he gave in to despair. Now he means to avenge Sif and free the titans' sacred grounds from his brother's madness.

title: Loken
body: Loken is the master of Ulduar, a keeper of the titans who has taken the city for himself. When he seized it he expelled the earthen who had built and tended it, and he sent his favorite servants, the iron dwarves, on a brutal campaign against all the creatures of stone. They have hunted the exiles relentlessly ever since, and wherever the stormforged march across the peaks, they march in his name.

parts.body: At the Temple of Wisdom, Loken revealed a deeper deceit. Lok'lira the Crone, the frail prisoner of the Forlorn Mine who set Thorim's awakening in motion, was his illusion. He had waited for weeks in that mine for a champion bold enough to rouse his brother and draw him away from the Temple of Storms, where Thorim was strongest, to fight close to the power of Loken's own master.

title: Brann Bronzebeard
body: Brann Bronzebeard, the famed explorer of the Explorers' League and a brother of King Magni of Ironforge, has come to the Storm Peaks on the trail of Ulduar, and no one quite knows where he is. The secrets of the titans have drawn him north across Northrend, and his own notes point to these mountains. Those who would find him, friend or not, must start from his camp at the foot of titan ruins above the frozen Bor's Breath River.

parts.body: His camp was found deserted, iron dwarves prowling where he had worked and only a note left behind. A tracking beast followed the scent from the camp to his stolen belongings and his communicator, and through it Brann himself appeared, alive and plainly surprised to see who had found him.

title: King Jokkum
body: King Jokkum rules the Sons of Hodir from Dun Niffelem, a frost giant who listens patiently and weighs every request before he answers. The death of Fjorn earned its bringer a hearing, but the bad blood between his people and Thorim runs deep, and his first answer to the Stormlord's envoy was a measured one: as payment for the help against Fjorn, he let Njormeld reforge the armor the giants gave Thorim ages ago, and no more.

parts.body: Jokkum remembers the dark day at Thunderfall that divides his people from Thorim. The frozen fossils there and the spirits that haunt the place keep it alive, and he believes his people will never forgive the Stormlord until something takes the place of those images: a memorial, built from the shattered pieces of Hodir's Horn.

title: Bouldercrag the Rockshaper
body: Bouldercrag the Rockshaper leads the earthen driven out of Ulduar, holding out at the refuge that bears his name. He remembers when his people's hammers hewed stone instead of iron; since their expulsion the weakest of them have died and the strongest craftsmen have been reborn as warriors. His defenders are hardy but not tireless, and he counts every one who falls, yet the hammers of the earthen stand united behind him, and any friend of the earthen is welcome at his side.

parts.body: Those who come to the refuge in Brann Bronzebeard's name find a warm welcome. Bouldercrag counts the explorer the closest ally his people have among those of flesh, a brother to the earthen in their struggle against Loken and his followers and in the fight to win back Ulduar.

body: Ricket is a goblin of K3 with a grin for every explosion and a plan for every problem, most of them loud. She keeps the town's sapper squad ready, lays Jeer Sparksocket's new mines in the path of the magnataur of Garm, and sends newcomers out for food, for K3 has grown more popular than anyone planned for. She thinks herself brilliant and is never shy about saying so, and even Jeer warns that she is a little loopy.

parts.body: Even Ricket admits that K3 will not win a foothold deeper in the peaks: freezing engines, vrykul women, territorial drakes and half a dozen other nasties have seen to that. One-way trips are another matter, and her rockets, the D16 Propelled Delivery Devices, fling the willing over the mountains.

title: Creteus
body: Creteus keeps watch over the Engine of the Makers from the Foot Steppes, the one the frostborn call the keeper. He speaks with grave courtesy and favors visitors who use their tongues before their blades, a quality he finds ever rarer among mortals. The hermit Drom Frostgrip spoke with him often and believed that what Creteus left unsaid gave away the secrets he guarded. He helps no one blindly, and asks first what a seeker truly wants.

parts.body: Creteus is troubled. He has learned that the seat of the watcher Thorim is contested and his fate uncertain, and the databank he sent to the temples of the Terrace of the Makers found the other watchers gone from them. What befell them he cannot say, but he fears their absence spells dark times for all of Azeroth.

title: Xarantaur
body: Xarantaur calls himself the Witness. He was among the first tauren druids, of the last generation taught by Cenarius when the world was young, and where his kin hunted great beasts he hunted stories. He has come to Camp Tunka'lo to learn more of Stormhoof, a taunka hero whose battle against the North Wind he heard of from Wind Tamer Barah in the Borean Tundra, but the people of Tunka'lo seem to know nothing of him.

parts.body: Tunka'lo's own scrolls told Stormhoof's tale differently, as a villain's, and the Lorehammer that Nozdormu gave Xarantaur when the bronze dragonflight made him immortal stirred at it: time has gone awry here. Even the spirit of Chieftain Swiftspear, Stormhoof's brother, is losing his memories of the hero, and the Witness means to restore the true history.

title: The Hyldsmeet
body: Deep in the Forlorn Mine, chained among the Hyldnir's captives, sits Lok'lira the Crone, who says that among her people she is known as a Yrkvinn, a weaver of illusions. She guesses at once that a stranger has come for the goblin prisoner, Zeev Fizzlespark, and offers a bargain. No one will get him out by force, not alive, but with her runes she could make her rescuer pass unnoticed among the Hyldnir. The runes are in the keeping of Overseer Syra, who patrols the mine, and Lok'lira says she dreads what will become of her if she stays a prisoner much longer.

parts.body: Wearing her illusion, the stranger served Mildred the Cruel as a new overseer, driving exhausted vrykul men back to work and slaying Garhal, who had been stirring talk of revolt. Satisfied, Mildred handed over the key to the shackles of a troublesome prisoner, to be quietly killed: Lok'lira herself, whose crime was to claim a place in the Hyldsmeet.

Then Lok'lira told her purpose: Thorim lost his wife to his brother's treachery and turned on the frost giants, and she wants him roused to retake Ulduar before the world is torn asunder.

title: The Stormlord's Atonement
body: Roused at last, Thorim means to take back the Terrace of the Makers from his brother, but he cannot do it alone, and the allies he needs are the ones he wronged. As a first step toward mending fences with the frost giants of Dun Niffelem, he would strike at their common enemy: Fjorn, whose giants of iron besiege the giants' city from Fjorn's Anvil in the east. To his envoy he gives a charm that calls his earthen to fight alongside.

parts.body: Among the wreckage of Fjorn's iron giants lay a strange, slag-covered metal, and the anvil's fire, fed with sparks torn from the revenants, burned it clean: hard but not brittle, far lighter than it looked, and marked with one of Thorim's runes. It was what remained of his own armor, cast off in grief long ago, and only the Sons of Hodir who made it could reforge it.

title: The Reckoning
body: With his armor restored, Thorim prepares to strike at his brother's army, and for that he needs a mount. Years ago he released his riding drake, Veranus, into the wild, and she returned to lead her own brood. She is long past breeding now, but out of sheer pride she still guards her old, empty nest. Thorim has a plan to bring her back, if someone will steal him eggs from the other proto-drake nests near Brunnhildar and set them where she will see.

parts.body: The stolen eggs were laid in her nest, and Veranus came down roaring to defend it. Thorim dropped onto her back from above and mastered her once more, calling her his old friend, and for the first time in years he felt his luck turning.

title: The Sons of Hodir
body: The frost giants of Dun Niffelem call themselves the Sons of Hodir, and they look to Hodir for protection and guidance. Outsiders earn their regard slowly, by deeds. Their smith Njormeld has drawn up plans for an artifact that will bring Hodir's blessing of protection to the stronghold, and needs only the eyes of their fallen iron foes to finish it. The giants treasure everfrost, ice that never melts, as the symbol of their people's heart, though over the ages the jormungar have devoured nearly all of it.

parts.body: The helm was forged and raised: Hodir's Helm now crowns an ice spike in Dun Niffelem, and with it the stronghold will be warned of danger before it arrives. The honor of reading its pronouncement to the king and his people went to an outsider, a thing never granted before.

parts.body: Lorekeeper Randvir received a vision from Hodir himself revealing the secret of a great artifact, and warned that doom would follow if the gift were refused. From everfrost shards gathered in the depths of the Hibernal Cavern and the hides of stoic mammoths, Hodir's Spear was raised in Dun Niffelem, a prophecy fulfilled.

title: The Iron Colossus
body: The stormforged war golems of Nidavelir wear plates of armor too thick and too large for them, bolted on like a crude upgrade, and the earthen can hardly bear the metal: even its presence brings Bruor Ironbane pain. Runeseer Valduran has spent an extraordinary effort mining, refining, smithing and testing it. Bruor suspects one of the runeseer's schemes and wants to know what the plates are really for, and whether the attendants of Mimir's old workshop can still tell him.

parts.body: Attendant Tock found the plate to be saronite alloyed with iron, from ore that came from deep in the crust of Azeroth and could only have been made by a powerful, malevolent force. Its records were sealed in Ulduar's archives by order of Keeper Loken, but the plate's size and bolt holes spoke plainly: armor for something colossal, meant for the final strike against the refuge.

parts.body: Valduran the Stormborn was hunted down in Nidavelir, with Bouldercrag and Bruor fighting at his attacker's side, and he died there. Before he fell he scoffed at the earthen and boasted that nothing they did could prevent the completion of the iron colossus.

Overseer Narvir reached it first, and with the heart in his hands the colossus would come to its full power.

Driven by an ally of the refuge, a jormungar tamed by the earthen handlers brought the iron colossus down, and the refuge was saved.

title: Norgannon's Keystone
body: Brann Bronzebeard has a lead on Norgannon's keystone, which guards the way into Ulduar's archives. The titans split it in two and hid the halves. The first, the keystone's shell, is held in the Inventor's Library, Keeper Mimir's hall on the northern coast south of Ulduar, and it is reached with an inventor's disk assembled from fragments the library's guardians carry. Brann works through his communicator while he hunts for the other half himself, and he guides each step from afar.

parts.body: The disk came out blank, but carried among the library's databanks it filled with Mimir's hidden data, and the library's console greeted it as Keeper Mimir himself. Charged, the disk woke Archivist Mechaton, guardian of the shell, and the first half of the keystone was taken from it.
sources: quests 12860/12927, 13415/13416, 12872/12928 descriptions and reward text

parts.body: The core was harder to find. Lagnus read its shape from the shell, King Stormheart's challenge led to the hermit Drom Frostgrip, and Drom's ring won a hearing from Creteus. Satisfied that Brann sought the keystone for a worthy end, and perhaps was the very one it was made for, Creteus named its resting place, the Frigid Tomb, and the core was found there in a sealed chest.
sources: quests 12871, 12873, 12874, 12875, 12877, 12878 descriptions and reward text

parts.body: The Explorers' League camp that bore Brann's name had been ruined by iron dwarves, but the prospectors' maps and notes survived. Soren's notes named the core's keeper, Athan, one of Mimir's creations, in a vault now called Loken's Bargain above the Valley of Ancient Winters, and the core was won from him.
sources: quests 13273, 13274 descriptions and reward text

parts.body: Shell and core were joined at last, with Brann himself there to see it, and Norgannon's keystone was whole. The key to Ulduar's archives, which he had chased across the peaks, was in his hands, and Brann could hardly contain his excitement at what might wait within.

title: The Brothers Bronzebeard
body: Yorg Stormheart, King of the Frostborn, is held by his people to be the wisest and strongest leader they have known, and he has trained them into fearsome warriors. His peachy skin sets him apart from those he rules. Lagnus of the Explorers' League urges courtesy toward him, for he is deeply respected. The king will not force his people into outsiders' affairs, but he offers the League their aid if its champion proves as strong and fierce as any frostborn.

parts.body: Velog Icebellow told the tale on the way to the test. Years ago, frostborn crossing from the Dragonblight in a terrible blizzard found a mountain dwarf wandering in bloodied snow with no memory of his name. When a jormungar struck, the stranger grew, his skin turned to stone and lightning sizzled at his hands, and he slew it with a hurled hammer. They named him Yorg, a name kept for champions of legend.
sources: creature_text 30401 groups 2-9

parts.body: At Frosthold, Brann Bronzebeard knew the king at once: Yorg Stormheart was his brother Muradin, long thought dead. His memories began to return, and King Magni, who had come to Northrend to find him, greeted him there. Muradin remembered Arthas, and how he had watched the prince turn and done nothing, and he set out alone to make Arthas answer for what he has done.
